description: TypeScript type system, inference, narrowing, generics, utility types, discriminated unions, and strict configuration archetypes.

archetypes.name: Public Boundary Annotation & Local Inference Balance
archetypes.coreConcept: Annotating exported function parameters and return types to lock public module contracts while letting TypeScript infer local variables and intermediate expressions cleanly.
mentalModel: 1. Annotate every function parameter (TypeScript cannot infer parameter types without call-site context).
2. Annotate public/exported function return types so accidental implementation changes fail at the boundary.
3. Let local variables and intermediate expressions be inferred from their initializers unless a wider union or empty collection needs an explicit type.
archetypes.governingInvariant: publicBoundary(params: ExplicitTypes): ExplicitReturnType with zero 'any' types

cognitiveTraps.name: Implicit or Explicit Any Parameter
cognitiveTraps.description: Omitting parameter types under strict mode or falling back to ': any' disables type checking at the function boundary.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function formatTotal(amount) { ... } fails TS7006; changing to (amount: any) silently accepts strings.

cognitiveTraps.name: Missing Exported Return Annotation
cognitiveTraps.description: Omitting the return type on an exported function allows a refactored return statement to silently change the public contract.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Returning null on an early exit widens inferred return from number to number | null without warning callers at the definition.

cognitiveTraps.name: Unannotated Empty Array Inference
cognitiveTraps.description: Initializing 'const items = []' without an annotation infers 'never[]' (or 'any[]' under noImplicitAny: false), failing when pushing typed elements.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const tags = []; tags.push('ok'); fails in strict mode or leaks any[].

realWorldDomains.description: Calculating line-item subtotals and tax rates in a strictly typed billing module.
Evaluating typed user attributes against rollout percentages.

qualityChecks.check: Module parameters, local bindings, and return types never use `any` (explicit or implicit); unknown inputs use `unknown` or concrete types.
qualityChecks.why: Using `any` disables TypeScript's type checker and propagates unsoundness to every caller.

qualityChecks.check: Exported functions declare explicit parameter and return type annotations while keeping trivial local initializers inferred.
qualityChecks.why: Explicit boundary signatures catch accidental contract drift at the function definition rather than in distant callers.

archetypes.name: Literal Widening, Const Narrowing & Contextual Typing
archetypes.coreConcept: Controlling how TypeScript widens mutable bindings and object properties versus preserving narrow literal types with 'const', 'as const', and contextual parameter typing.
mentalModel: 1. 'const x = "GET"' infers the literal type '"GET"', whereas 'let x = "GET"' widens to 'string' because 'let' can be reassigned.
2. 'const obj = { method: "GET" }' widens 'obj.method' to 'string' because object properties remain mutable unless frozen with 'as const' or typed explicitly.
3. Callback parameters inside typed array methods (e.g. items.map(item => ...)) are contextually typed and do not need redundant annotations.
archetypes.governingInvariant: literalBinding preserves exact literal/union type without widening to string/number

cognitiveTraps.name: Object Property Literal Widening
cognitiveTraps.description: Passing a property of an unannotated 'const obj = { mode: "fast" }' to a function expecting '"fast" | "safe"' fails because 'obj.mode' widened to 'string'.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const req = { method: 'GET' }; send(req.method); // Error: string not assignable to 'GET' | 'POST'

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutable Let Literal Widening
cognitiveTraps.description: Initializing a variable with 'let' instead of 'const' (or without a union annotation) widens its type to 'string' or 'number', breaking literal parameter calls.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: let role = 'viewer'; assignRole(role); // Error: string is not assignable to 'viewer' | 'editor'

cognitiveTraps.name: Redundant or Mismatched Callback Annotation
cognitiveTraps.description: Annotating callback parameters with ': any' or an imprecise type overrides TypeScript's contextual typing from the source array.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: users.map((u: any) => u.name.toUpperCase()) loses property checking.

realWorldDomains.description: Building typed HTTP request descriptors and retry policies with literal method and backoff modes.
Routing typed log severity levels ('info' | 'warn' | 'error') without literal widening.

qualityChecks.check: Configuration literals and constants passed to literal-typed boundaries preserve narrow types via `const`, `as const`, or explicit type annotations rather than type assertions.
qualityChecks.why: Widening a literal property to `string` or `number` forces unsafe `as` casts or compiler errors at call sites.

qualityChecks.check: Callback parameters in typed higher-order methods rely on contextual typing rather than `any` annotations.
qualityChecks.why: Contextual typing automatically propagates element types through `.map`/`.filter`/`.reduce` with zero boilerplate.

archetypes.name: Type Annotation & Inference Bug Diagnosis
archetypes.coreConcept: Diagnosing why TypeScript infers an unexpected type (widened primitive, never[], or any leak from JSON.parse) and fixing it with clean annotations rather than unsafe 'as' assertions.
mentalModel: 1. Trace what TypeScript infers at each binding: const literal vs let widened vs object property widened.
2. Replace 'any' leaks (especially from unannotated parameters or JSON.parse) with explicit boundary types or 'unknown'.
3. Fix the root declaration or boundary signature instead of masking errors with 'as' casts.
archetypes.governingInvariant: zero 'any' leaks and zero unsafe 'as' casts across refactored or debugged modules

cognitiveTraps.name: Masking Type Errors with Unsafe Assertions
cognitiveTraps.description: Using 'value as TargetType' silences the compiler without verifying or fixing the widened or mismatched type.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const raw = getInput(); return raw as UserConfig; hides missing fields at runtime.

cognitiveTraps.name: JSON.parse Any Propagation
cognitiveTraps.description: Returning 'JSON.parse(raw)' directly from a function without a boundary check leaks 'any' to every caller.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function loadConfig(raw: string) { return JSON.parse(raw); } infers return type 'any'.

realWorldDomains.description: Parsing and validating application environment settings without 'any' leaks.
Refactoring loosely typed log formatters into strict TypeScript modules.

qualityChecks.check: Type errors are resolved through accurate parameter/return annotations, `as const`, or `unknown` checks rather than `as any` or unchecked `as` casts.
qualityChecks.why: Unchecked assertions bypass TypeScript's static guarantees and hide runtime mismatches.

qualityChecks.check: External unparsed data (`JSON.parse` or raw inputs) is typed as `unknown` at the boundary and checked before returning a typed value.
qualityChecks.why: `JSON.parse` returns `any` by default, silently disabling type safety if returned directly.

archetypes.name: Immutable Domain Entity Contracts
archetypes.coreConcept: Use object types and readonly members to describe stable entity identity and the fields callers may update.
mentalModel: 1. Identify which values define identity and should not change after construction.
2. Mark stable properties readonly at the type boundary.
3. Keep runtime immutability separate from TypeScript's compile-time readonly check.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A caller cannot reassign an entity's stable identifiers through its declared type.

cognitiveTraps.name: Mutable Entity Identity
cognitiveTraps.description: An entity identifier remains assignable, allowing different code paths to silently change which record an object represents.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Assign a replacement id through a shared entity reference and observe that downstream lookups now target a different record.

cognitiveTraps.name: Shallow Readonly Assumption
cognitiveTraps.description: A readonly outer property is mistaken for recursive immutability, even though its nested object or array remains mutable.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Keep a nested preferences object mutable beneath a readonly profile property and update its theme through the nested reference.

realWorldDomains.description: Model stable SKU identity with mutable display fields in an inventory catalog.
Separate stable customer identity from editable profile preferences.

qualityChecks.check: Stable domain identifiers are readonly at public object boundaries, and caller-owned input objects are not reassigned to change identity.
qualityChecks.why: Mutable identity makes caches, indexes, and references point at a different entity without an explicit transition.

knownBad.code:
type CatalogItem = { sku: string; label: string };
function renameItem(item: CatalogItem, nextSku: string) { item.sku = nextSku; }

qualityChecks.check: The type model makes the intended mutability of nested objects explicit instead of implying that a top-level readonly property freezes its contents.
qualityChecks.why: TypeScript readonly is shallow; callers can still mutate nested state unless nested members are also readonly.

knownBad.code:
type Customer = { readonly preferences: { theme: string } };
function setTheme(customer: Customer, theme: string) { customer.preferences.theme = theme; }

archetypes.name: Literal Domain Values & Const Inference
archetypes.coreConcept: Preserve specific string, numeric, and tuple values as literal types when they define a finite domain contract.
mentalModel: 1. Separate a domain's allowed values from arbitrary strings or numbers.
2. Use literal unions for named alternatives and `as const` for readonly literal data.
3. Widen a value only when the contract genuinely accepts the wider type.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A value used as a domain variant remains assignable only to the declared literal alternatives.

cognitiveTraps.name: Literal Value Widens to Primitive
cognitiveTraps.description: A value that should represent one of a finite set widens to string or number and loses its domain constraint.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Infer a mutable variable as string, then pass it to a function that accepts only named payment states.

cognitiveTraps.name: Configuration Tuple Widens and Mutates
cognitiveTraps.description: A fixed pair of configuration values is inferred as a general mutable array, losing both positional meaning and literal values.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass a mutable numeric array into a function that expects a readonly two-element bounds tuple.

realWorldDomains.description: Constrain currency, payment status, and settlement mode values in payment services.
Represent fixed minimum and maximum reorder thresholds as a readonly tuple.

qualityChecks.check: Finite domain alternatives retain their literal union type at the public boundary rather than widening to an unrestricted primitive.
qualityChecks.why: Widening admits values the business contract does not define and postpones errors until runtime.

knownBad.code:
type PaymentState = 'authorized' | 'settled' | 'voided';
function transition(next: string): PaymentState { return next as PaymentState; }

qualityChecks.check: Fixed domain constants and tuple positions preserve their literal values and readonly shape when used as configuration.
qualityChecks.why: Mutable widened arrays lose positional meaning and can be changed by unrelated callers.

archetypes.name: Object Shape & Construction Boundaries
archetypes.coreConcept: Model required and optional object properties deliberately, and understand when fresh object literals receive excess-property checks.
mentalModel: 1. Treat a type as a structural contract for the properties a consumer may rely on.
2. Mark a field optional only when its absence is a supported domain state.
3. Use typed construction boundaries to catch misspelled or unsupported fields early.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every accepted object shape represents a valid domain state, and unknown fields are not silently asserted into the contract.

cognitiveTraps.name: Fresh Literal Check Misunderstanding
cognitiveTraps.description: A learner assumes excess-property checking applies identically to a fresh object literal and a previously inferred variable.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass a variable with an extra misspelled optional field and compare it with the same shape passed inline.

cognitiveTraps.name: Optional Properties Hide Invalid Shapes
cognitiveTraps.description: Many unrelated optional properties allow incomplete or contradictory objects that are not meaningful domain states.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Construct a configuration object with none of its identifying fields and observe that the broad interface still accepts it.

realWorldDomains.description: Validate typed order-line objects imported from an internal catalog adapter.
Define valid option shapes for feature flag evaluation without typo-prone optional bags.

qualityChecks.check: Object shape mismatches are corrected at the construction boundary instead of hidden with unchecked type assertions.
qualityChecks.why: An assertion suppresses the exact structural error the contract is meant to catch.

knownBad.code:
type ImportRow = { sku: string; quantity: number };
const row = { sku: 'SKU-8', quntity: 2 } as ImportRow;

qualityChecks.check: Optional members correspond to genuinely absent domain data; required identity and discriminator fields remain required.
qualityChecks.why: Overly permissive shapes admit incomplete values and force callers to handle states that should not exist.

knownBad.code:
type DeliveryWindow = { start?: string; end?: string; timezone?: string };
const window: DeliveryWindow = {};

archetypes.name: Discriminated Domain Unions
archetypes.coreConcept: Represent mutually exclusive domain states as separate object types connected by a literal discriminant, then narrow before reading member-specific fields.
mentalModel: 1. Each union member is one valid domain state.
2. A shared literal discriminant identifies which member is present at runtime.
3. Narrow on that discriminant before accessing state-specific data.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Every state-specific field access is dominated by a check that narrows the value to the member declaring that field.

cognitiveTraps.name: Optional Property Bag for Exclusive States
cognitiveTraps.description: Modeling mutually exclusive states as one type with many optional fields permits contradictory or incomplete combinations.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: type Payment = { kind: string; authCode?: string; receiptId?: string; reason?: string };

cognitiveTraps.name: Member Field Access Before Narrowing
cognitiveTraps.description: Reading a property that exists on only some members before checking the discriminant violates the union guarantee.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function idOf(state: PaymentState) { return state.receiptId; }

realWorldDomains.description: Represent authorized, captured, and declined payment outcomes with distinct data.
Represent queued, processing, completed, and failed media jobs as explicit states.

qualityChecks.check: Read a member-specific field only after a valid discriminant or equivalent guard narrows the union to the declaring member.
qualityChecks.why: A union promises that one of its members is present, not that every member-specific property exists.

knownBad.code:
type PaymentState = { kind: 'captured'; receiptId: string } | { kind: 'declined'; reason: string };
function receipt(state: PaymentState): string { return state.receiptId; }

qualityChecks.check: Represent mutually exclusive domain states as separate object members instead of a loose object with unrelated optional state fields.
qualityChecks.why: Separate members make impossible combinations harder to construct and give each narrowed branch an accurate contract.

knownBad.code: type PaymentState = { kind: string; receiptId?: string; reason?: string };

archetypes.name: Exhaustive State Handlers
archetypes.coreConcept: Handle every member of a discriminated union and make additions to the domain state visible at the handler boundary.
mentalModel: 1. Narrow using the shared discriminant.
2. Give each state an explicit branch with its state-specific behavior.
3. Use a `never` check when the handler must fail compilation after a new member is added.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A handler accounts for every member in the declared union; exhaustive handlers use a never-typed remainder rather than silently treating it as a generic fallback.

cognitiveTraps.name: Silent Non-Exhaustive Default
cognitiveTraps.description: A broad default branch can accept a newly added state without implementing the required behavior.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: default: return 'unknown';

cognitiveTraps.name: Missing State Branch
cognitiveTraps.description: Omitting one current union member leaves it unhandled or routed through unrelated behavior.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: switch (job.kind) { case 'queued': return 'waiting'; case 'done': return 'ready'; }

realWorldDomains.description: Update status labels and actions for each processing lifecycle state.
Handle staged, loaded, dispatched, and cancelled orders exhaustively.

qualityChecks.check: Handle every declared discriminant member in a state handler, with a compile-time remainder check when future members must not fall through silently.
qualityChecks.why: A new state should cause the relevant handler to be revisited rather than inherit unrelated fallback behavior.

knownBad.code:
type JobState = { kind: 'queued' } | { kind: 'done' } | { kind: 'failed' };
function label(job: JobState): string { switch (job.kind) { case 'queued': return 'waiting'; case 'done': return 'ready'; default: return 'other'; } }

qualityChecks.check: Use a `never`-typed remainder or equivalent compile-time check when the handler's contract requires exhaustive coverage.
qualityChecks.why: The remainder becomes non-never when an unhandled member is added, producing a local compiler signal.

knownBad.code:
function assertNever(value: never): never { throw new Error(String(value)); }
function label(job: JobState): string { switch (job.kind) { case 'queued': return 'waiting'; default: return assertNever(job); } }

archetypes.name: Union Collection Shapes and Shared Members
archetypes.coreConcept: Distinguish an array containing a union of values from a union of homogeneous arrays, and use only members guaranteed across a union until narrowing.
mentalModel: 1. Parentheses determine whether the union is inside each array element or outside the whole array.
2. A union value exposes only members common to every alternative before narrowing.
3. Narrow the container or element according to the operation the domain needs.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The type groups values at the same level as the actual data contract: mixed elements use `(A | B)[]`; alternatives of homogeneous collections use `A[] | B[]`.

cognitiveTraps.name: Mixed Array vs. Union of Homogeneous Arrays
cognitiveTraps.description: Confusing `(A | B)[]` with `A[] | B[]` changes whether different element kinds can coexist.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: type Batch = string[] | number[]; const batch: Batch = ['ready', 3];

cognitiveTraps.name: Using a Non-Shared Member
cognitiveTraps.description: Calling a member available only on one union alternative without first narrowing is unsafe.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function size(value: string | number) { return value.length; }

realWorldDomains.description: Represent a batch of mixed typed telemetry values versus a batch whose entire payload uses one encoding.
Read shared ranking metadata before narrowing result variants to document or person records.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook: Everyday Types — Union Types

qualityChecks.check: Choose `(A | B)[]` for mixed element arrays and `A[] | B[]` for a collection that is wholly one element type, matching the stated data contract.
qualityChecks.why: The placement of the union changes which element sequences are representable and which array operations are safe.

knownBad.code:
type Batch = string[] | number[];
const mixed: Batch = ['sensor-7', 12];

qualityChecks.check: Before narrowing a union value, access only members present on every alternative.
qualityChecks.why: A value may be any member of the union, so a non-shared property is not guaranteed until a runtime check selects a member.

knownBad.code: function label(value: string | number): string { return value.toUpperCase(); }

archetypes.name: Safe Unknown Boundaries
archetypes.coreConcept: Keep external values as unknown and narrow them with runtime checks before property access or domain use.
mentalModel: 1. Treat external data as unknown at the boundary.
2. Check nullish and primitive cases before inspecting object members.
3. Return a domain value only after every required condition is established.
archetypes.governingInvariant: No property access or domain assertion occurs on unknown input until runtime checks establish the relevant shape.

cognitiveTraps.name: typeof Null Mistaken for a Non-Null Record
cognitiveTraps.description: `typeof value === 'object'` also accepts null, so a subsequent property operation may throw.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function hasId(value: unknown) { return typeof value === 'object' && 'id' in value; }

cognitiveTraps.name: Truthiness Confuses Zero with Missing
cognitiveTraps.description: A truthiness check rejects valid numeric zero even when the domain permits it.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if (typeof payload.amount === 'number' && payload.amount) return payload.amount;

realWorldDomains.description: Narrow JSON event data before reading shipment identifiers or status details.
Validate untrusted numeric adjustment data while preserving a valid zero amount.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook: Narrowing — typeof Type Guards and Truthiness Narrowing

qualityChecks.check: Exclude `null` (and arrays when the domain requires a plain record) before using the `in` operator or reading object properties from unknown input.
qualityChecks.why: The `typeof` result for null is `object`, and property inspection before a non-null check can throw at runtime.

knownBad.code: function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> { return typeof value === 'object' && 'id' in value; }

qualityChecks.check: Use an explicit type or nullish check when zero or an empty string is valid data; do not let truthiness collapse it into the missing case.
qualityChecks.why: A valid falsy value must retain its domain meaning instead of being treated as absent.

knownBad.code: function readAmount(amount: number | undefined): number { return amount ? amount : 100; }

archetypes.name: Complete Type Predicates for Domain Records
archetypes.coreConcept: A predicate returning `value is T` must establish every required field and value property promised by T.
mentalModel: 1. Validate the outer container and each required key.
2. Check each property's runtime type and any domain bounds.
3. Return true only when the whole predicate is supported by checks.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A true type-predicate result implies that all required fields of the target type have been checked at runtime.

cognitiveTraps.name: Marker-Only Type Predicate
cognitiveTraps.description: Checking one marker field and returning true can falsely certify an object that lacks other required fields.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function isAccount(value: unknown): value is Account { return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && 'kind' in value; }

cognitiveTraps.name: Inherited Property Accepted as Own Data
cognitiveTraps.description: Using `in` alone accepts properties inherited from the prototype when the payload contract requires own fields.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: if ('accountId' in value) return true;

realWorldDomains.description: Check required fields and value types before accepting partner-provided account records.
Convert untrusted notices into a typed shipment event only after full validation.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook: Narrowing — User-Defined Type Predicates

qualityChecks.check: A type predicate checks each required property and its runtime type before returning true.
qualityChecks.why: TypeScript trusts a predicate's return annotation; an incomplete predicate can make unsafe property access appear valid everywhere downstream.

knownBad.code:
type Account = { accountId: string; active: boolean };
function isAccount(value: unknown): value is Account { return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && 'accountId' in value; }

qualityChecks.check: Use an own-property check when the input contract requires data fields supplied directly on the payload rather than inherited from its prototype.
qualityChecks.why: The `in` operator searches the prototype chain and may accept an object that does not carry the field as its own payload data.

knownBad.code: function hasOwnId(value: object): boolean { return 'id' in value; }

archetypes.name: Preserve Generic Input and Output Relationships
archetypes.coreConcept: A useful generic type parameter captures a concrete caller type and carries it through a reusable function's inputs and outputs.
mentalModel: 1. Let the call site's values provide evidence for a type parameter.
2. Reuse that parameter in the public contract wherever the same type relationship must hold.
3. Keep the returned type specific enough for callers to use without assertions.
archetypes.governingInvariant: The public signature preserves the input/output relationship that callers rely on instead of widening useful results to unknown or a broad record type.

cognitiveTraps.name: Widening a Useful Result
cognitiveTraps.description: A generic input is accepted, but the return type is widened so callers lose the concrete type captured at the call site.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass an array of a domain union to a reusable selector and verify the result still has that union type plus the empty-case value.

cognitiveTraps.name: Using a Type Parameter Without a Relationship
cognitiveTraps.description: A type parameter appears only once and adds no caller-visible relationship, making the signature look more precise than it is.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Replace a generic formatting helper's parameter with unknown and verify that its accepted inputs and return contract do not change.

realWorldDomains.description: Project a typed field from invoice rows while preserving the selected field's value type.
Select the first state from a typed notification queue while modeling the empty case.

qualityChecks.check: Public generic signatures preserve a caller-visible relationship between input and output types instead of widening the result unnecessarily.
qualityChecks.why: Callers lose compile-time guarantees when a reusable helper discards the specific type inferred from its arguments.

knownBad.code: function first<T>(items: readonly T[]): unknown { return items[0]; }

qualityChecks.check: Each type parameter contributes a useful relationship among parameters, properties, callbacks, or the return type.
qualityChecks.why: An unused type parameter adds apparent complexity without improving what callers can safely do.

knownBad.code: function formatValue<T>(value: T): string { return String(value); }

archetypes.name: Constrain Reusable Property Access
archetypes.coreConcept: Generic constraints state the minimum capabilities an implementation needs, and key constraints connect a selected property to its corresponding value type.
mentalModel: 1. Identify the property capability the implementation actually uses.
2. Express that capability as a constraint without imposing unrelated domain requirements.
3. When a caller supplies a key, restrict it to keys of the input and derive the result from that key.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A generic operation reads only properties guaranteed by its constraint and preserves the selected property's type for valid keys.

cognitiveTraps.name: Accepting an Arbitrary String as a Key
cognitiveTraps.description: A generic field helper accepts keys that are not known to exist on the input and hides the lost relationship behind unknown or a broad lookup.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Call the helper with a valid numeric field and then a misspelled key; the valid call should retain its numeric result type and the misspelling should be rejected.

cognitiveTraps.name: Adding an Unneeded Domain Constraint
cognitiveTraps.description: A reusable helper requires a specific identifier shape even though its implementation uses no identifier and could support other valid domain values.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass both a string-keyed and number-keyed record to a helper that only returns the original record; both should satisfy the intended contract.

realWorldDomains.description: Read a chosen typed field from catalog entries without accepting keys that are absent from the entry shape.
Adapt pages with different item types while preserving the item and cursor types used by each caller.

archetypes.source: TypeScript Handbook — Generics and keyof types: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/generics.html

qualityChecks.check: Constraints guarantee every member the implementation reads, while accepting all domain inputs covered by the stated contract.
qualityChecks.why: An insufficient constraint forces unsafe access; an unnecessarily narrow constraint rejects valid callers and makes a reusable helper brittle.

knownBad.code: function keep<T extends { id: string }>(record: T): T { return record; }

qualityChecks.check: A key parameter is restricted to properties of its input, and the result type remains tied to the selected property's value type.
qualityChecks.why: A broad string key or unknown result lets misspellings through and makes callers cast values the function could have typed precisely.

knownBad.code: function readField<T extends object>(record: T, key: string): unknown { return Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(record, key)?.value; }

archetypes.name: Derive Create and Update DTOs Safely
archetypes.coreConcept: Utility types derive request and response shapes from a canonical domain type so field names and value types stay synchronized while operation-specific rules exclude or relax only the intended fields.
mentalModel: 1. Start from the canonical domain entity rather than duplicating its fields.
2. Remove server-managed fields from create and update contracts.
3. Make only the editable update fields optional; Partial is shallow unless a nested patch is designed separately.
archetypes.governingInvariant: Create and update DTOs remain derived from the source entity, and an update patch never admits server-managed identity or creation fields.

cognitiveTraps.name: Making Managed Fields Optional Instead of Excluding Them
cognitiveTraps.description: Partial<T> makes every source property optional, including identifiers and server-owned timestamps, so those fields remain assignable in an update payload.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Build an update patch for a record with id, createdAt, title, and price; verify that id and createdAt are not accepted as editable patch properties.

cognitiveTraps.name: Treating Partial as Deep
cognitiveTraps.description: Partial<T> makes only top-level properties optional; a nested object that is included must still satisfy its declared shape.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Use a nested address object with required fields and confirm that an update contract does not accidentally accept a partial address unless a nested patch type is explicitly defined.

realWorldDomains.description: Derive create and update request DTOs from product records while preventing changes to generated identifiers and creation timestamps.
Model a profile patch that permits editable top-level fields and makes nested update policy explicit.

qualityChecks.check: Create and update DTO properties derive from the canonical domain type so source fields and value types do not drift across duplicated interfaces.
qualityChecks.why: Duplicated field lists can silently fall out of sync when the domain model changes.

knownBad.code: type Product = { id: string; createdAt: string; name: string; price: number }; type CreateProduct = { name: string; price: number };

qualityChecks.check: Update payloads exclude server-managed identity and creation fields instead of merely making every source property optional.
qualityChecks.why: A partial update must not let callers overwrite values owned by persistence or server-side creation.

knownBad.code: type Product = { id: string; createdAt: string; name: string; price: number }; type ProductPatch = Partial<Product>;

qualityChecks.check: Nested update behavior is explicit; Partial is treated as a top-level transformation unless a separate nested patch contract is defined.
qualityChecks.why: Assuming recursive optionality can make nested replacements incomplete or ambiguous.

knownBad.code: type Profile = { name: string; preferences: { email: boolean; sms: boolean } }; type ProfilePatch = Partial<Profile>;

archetypes.name: Build Exhaustive Maps from Finite Key Unions
archetypes.coreConcept: Record<KeyUnion, Value> constructs a map whose key space is the declared finite union and whose values share the specified type.
mentalModel: 1. Define the finite set of domain keys as a literal union.
2. Use the union as Record keys so every member must be represented.
3. Keep the value type tied to the map contract and update the map when the union grows.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A map for a finite domain union contains every declared key with a value that satisfies the domain value contract.

cognitiveTraps.name: Making an Exhaustive Map Partial
cognitiveTraps.description: Partial<Record<K, V>> allows a key from the finite union to be absent, hiding missing labels or handlers.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Extend a status union with one member and verify that the label map is forced to provide its entry.

cognitiveTraps.name: Replacing a Finite Key Set with Arbitrary Strings
cognitiveTraps.description: Record<string, V> accepts keys outside the domain union and loses compile-time protection when domain values change.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: Pass a map with a misspelled status key and verify the declared finite key contract rejects it.

realWorldDomains.description: Map each supported order status to a user-facing label used by an operations dashboard.
Associate every event kind in a finite transport event union with a typed handler.

qualityChecks.check: A Record keyed by a finite domain union represents every union member and does not make required entries optional.
qualityChecks.why: Missing map entries otherwise surface later as undefined labels or unhandled cases.

knownBad.code: type OrderStatus = "pending" | "paid" | "shipped"; type StatusLabels = Partial<Record<OrderStatus, string>>;

qualityChecks.check: The map key type stays tied to the declared domain union instead of widening to arbitrary strings.
qualityChecks.why: A finite key contract rejects misspelled or unsupported values and keeps call sites aligned with the domain.

knownBad.code: type OrderStatus = "pending" | "paid" | "shipped"; type StatusLabels = Record<string, string>;

archetypes.name: Explicit Result Variants and Safe Narrowing
archetypes.coreConcept: Represent mutually exclusive API outcomes as separate object variants with one shared literal field, then narrow by that field before using variant-specific data.
mentalModel: 1. Each object variant describes one valid outcome and the data that outcome owns.
2. The common literal field identifies which outcome arrived.
3. A branch on that field narrows the whole object before reading its payload.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A member-specific field is read only after the shared literal discriminant has narrowed the value to the variant that declares it.

cognitiveTraps.name: Optional Property Bag for Exclusive Outcomes
cognitiveTraps.description: One object with a broad string state and optional success/error payloads permits contradictory combinations that do not correspond to any valid outcome.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: type Result = { state: string; value?: Invoice; message?: string };

cognitiveTraps.name: Reading Payload Before Narrowing
cognitiveTraps.description: Reading a field that exists on only one result variant before checking the discriminant assumes that every result carries that field.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function valueOf(result: Result) { return result.value; }

realWorldDomains.description: Represent a shipment lookup that may be loading, found, or not found, with state-specific data.
Represent accepted and rejected rows from a catalog import with distinct payloads.

qualityChecks.check: Read a member-specific field only after a valid literal discriminant or equivalent guard narrows the union to the member that declares the field.
qualityChecks.why: A union guarantees one declared member is present, not that every variant-specific payload exists.

knownBad.code:
type ShipmentResult = { kind: 'found'; trackingCode: string } | { kind: 'missing'; reason: string };
function label(result: ShipmentResult): string { return result.trackingCode; }

qualityChecks.check: Represent mutually exclusive outcomes as separate union members instead of unrelated optional payload fields on a broad object.
qualityChecks.why: Separate variants prevent impossible combinations and let the compiler describe the payload available in each state.

knownBad.code: type ImportResult = { state: string; acceptedRows?: number; rejectionReason?: string };

archetypes.name: Exhaustive Result Handlers with Never
archetypes.coreConcept: Handle every declared result variant explicitly and make a newly added variant visible at the handler boundary through a never-typed remainder.
mentalModel: 1. Branch on the shared literal discriminant.
2. Give each current variant behavior that matches its contract.
3. Pass the remaining value to an assertNever helper so a future variant fails compilation until handled.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A handler covers every declared discriminant value; when exhaustive handling is required, its default remainder has type never.

cognitiveTraps.name: Silent Unknown-State Fallback
cognitiveTraps.description: A broad default branch silently routes a newly added outcome to generic behavior instead of forcing an explicit decision.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: default: return 'Unknown';

cognitiveTraps.name: Omitted Current Variant
cognitiveTraps.description: Leaving a currently declared variant out of a handler causes it to fall through or receive unrelated behavior.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: switch (result.kind) { case 'queued': return 'Waiting'; default: return assertNever(result); }

realWorldDomains.description: Update inventory review, approval, and release states through a reducer that must handle every action.
Render queued, approved, rejected, and withdrawn document review events.

qualityChecks.check: Provide behavior for every current discriminant member and avoid routing a new domain member through a generic fallback.
qualityChecks.why: Each new state may need distinct business behavior; a generic default can make the type model and behavior diverge.

knownBad.code:
type Review = { kind: 'queued' } | { kind: 'approved' } | { kind: 'rejected' };
function label(review: Review): string { switch (review.kind) { case 'queued': return 'Waiting'; case 'approved': return 'Done'; default: return 'Other'; } }

qualityChecks.check: Use a never-typed remainder or equivalent compile-time check when the handler contract requires exhaustive coverage.
qualityChecks.why: When a new union member is added, the remainder ceases to be never and points to the exact handler that needs an update.

knownBad.code:
function assertNever(value: never): never { throw new Error(String(value)); }
function label(review: Review): string { switch (review.kind) { case 'queued': return 'Waiting'; default: return assertNever(review); } }

archetypes.name: Strict Nullable Boundaries
archetypes.coreConcept: With strict null checking, represent absence in the type and narrow `null` or `undefined` before using a value that may be absent.
mentalModel: 1. Treat `null` and `undefined` as distinct values rather than assuming they fit every type.
2. Include an absence value in the type only when the contract allows it.
3. Check for the absence case before using the remaining value.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A value is used as present only after a guard has removed every allowed absence case from its type.

cognitiveTraps.name: Non-null Assertion Hides a Missing Value
cognitiveTraps.description: A postfix non-null assertion suppresses the compiler warning but does not add a runtime check, so missing data can still throw.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function label(name: string | null): string { return name!.trim(); }

cognitiveTraps.name: Null and Undefined Are Not Interchangeable
cognitiveTraps.description: A contract that permits only one absence value should not silently treat the other as present or valid data.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: const value: string | null = undefined;

realWorldDomains.description: Format a profile field that may be explicitly null when a member has no verified contact detail.
Format an optional delivery note while handling missing values without unsafe assertions.

qualityChecks.check: Before using a value that may be null or undefined, narrow every absence case permitted by its declared type or return a deliberate absence result.
qualityChecks.why: A type check cannot guarantee presence when the value contract still includes an absence case.

knownBad.code: function contactLabel(email: string | null): string { return email.trim(); }

qualityChecks.check: Do not use a non-null assertion to silence a missing-value path when the function contract allows the value to be absent.
qualityChecks.why: The assertion changes the compiler view but leaves the runtime value unchanged.

knownBad.code: function contactLabel(email: string | undefined): string { return email!.trim(); }

archetypes.name: Checked Array and Record Access
archetypes.coreConcept: An array index or open index-signature lookup may not find a value; `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` exposes that possibility as `undefined` so the code must handle it.
mentalModel: 1. A numeric index or open record key does not prove an entry exists.
2. Handle `undefined` before using the retrieved value.
3. Preserve empty string, zero, or false when present; only absence takes the missing-value path.
archetypes.governingInvariant: An indexed value is used only after its presence is established; a present falsy value is not treated as missing.

cognitiveTraps.name: Assumed Array or Record Entry
cognitiveTraps.description: Treating an indexed lookup as definitely present makes an empty collection or missing key trigger a runtime error.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function firstLabel(labels: readonly string[]): string { return labels[0].trim(); }

cognitiveTraps.name: Assuming Strict Includes Unchecked Index Checks
cognitiveTraps.description: The `strict` family does not automatically enable `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, so an unchecked lookup may still be typed as present.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: {"compilerOptions":{"strict":true}} // indexed reads still require presence handling

cognitiveTraps.name: A Present Empty String Is Still Present
cognitiveTraps.description: Using truthiness to test an indexed string conflates a present empty string with an absent key and silently changes valid data into the missing-value result.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function readNote(notes: Record<string, string>, key: string): string | undefined { const note = notes[key]; return note ? note.trim() : undefined; }

realWorldDomains.description: Read a named rollout flag where a key may not be present and false is a valid configured value.
Read a first keyword from a result list that can be empty.

qualityChecks.check: Check that an array or index-signature lookup found a value before calling value-specific methods or returning it as definitely present.
qualityChecks.why: Valid indexes and open record keys can be absent at runtime even when the container itself exists.

knownBad.code: function firstKeyword(words: readonly string[]): string { return words[0].trim(); }

qualityChecks.check: Distinguish a missing indexed value from a present empty string, zero, or false rather than using truthiness as the presence test.
qualityChecks.why: Falsy values can be legitimate data and must not be replaced with a missing-value fallback.

knownBad.code: function flagValue(flags: Record<string, boolean>, key: string): boolean { return flags[key] || true; }

archetypes.name: Unknown API Payload Boundary
archetypes.coreConcept: External JSON is data at runtime, not a trusted domain object; keep it as unknown until every required field has been checked.
mentalModel: 1. Treat decoded wire data as an untrusted value.
2. Narrow containers before reading properties.
3. Validate each field before constructing a domain value.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A domain value is returned only after runtime checks establish every invariant promised by its type.

cognitiveTraps.name: Assertion Mistaken for Validation
cognitiveTraps.description: A type assertion changes only the compiler view and does not verify the runtime payload.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function readProfile(payload: unknown): Profile { return payload as Profile; }

cognitiveTraps.name: Container Check Without Field Checks
cognitiveTraps.description: Confirming that a payload is an object does not prove that required properties have the expected runtime types.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: function readProfile(payload: unknown): Profile { if (typeof payload === "object" && payload !== null) return payload as Profile; throw new TypeError(); }

realWorldDomains.description: Validate an external customer response before passing it to application code.
Reject malformed webhook fields before updating shipment state.

qualityChecks.check: Values typed unknown are narrowed to a suitable non-null object before their properties are read.
qualityChecks.why: Untrusted data can be null or a primitive, and property access can otherwise fail at runtime.

knownBad.code: function readProfile(payload: unknown): string { return (payload as { displayName: string }).displayName; }

qualityChecks.check: Every required field used to construct a domain value is checked against its runtime type before the value is returned.
qualityChecks.why: A valid object container may still carry absent or wrongly typed fields.

knownBad.code: function isProfile(payload: Record<string, unknown>): boolean { return typeof payload.id === "string"; }

archetypes.name: Typed API Result Boundary
archetypes.coreConcept: A typed API boundary separates transport failure, HTTP failure, and invalid payload from a validated success value, using return types that callers must handle.
mentalModel: 1. Keep transport data separate from domain data.
2. Return success only after status and payload validation both succeed.
3. Represent expected failure cases explicitly so callers can narrow them.
archetypes.governingInvariant: A successful result contains only validated domain data, and every expected failure has an explicit result variant.

cognitiveTraps.name: Collapse Success and Failure into One Optional Bag
cognitiveTraps.description: Independent optional success and error fields permit contradictory combinations and leave callers guessing which value exists.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: type ApiResult<T> = { data?: T; error?: string };

cognitiveTraps.name: Trust a Body Before Checking the Response Contract
cognitiveTraps.description: An error response may have a different body shape from a successful response and must not be cast to the success type.
cognitiveTraps.reproducer: async function loadProfile(response: Response): Promise<Profile> { return await response.json() as Profile; }

realWorldDomains.description: Return validated order data or an explicit HTTP, network, or payload error.
Map malformed or rejected webhook requests into deliberate caller-visible results.

qualityChecks.check: A success result is created only after all required response fields pass runtime validation.
qualityChecks.why: Static annotations cannot establish the shape of bytes received over the network.

knownBad.code: function ok<T>(payload: unknown): { ok: true; data: T } { return { ok: true, data: payload as T }; }

qualityChecks.check: Expected transport, status, or validation failures are returned as distinguishable outcomes rather than hidden in an ambiguous optional-property object.
qualityChecks.why: Callers need a reliable branch that identifies which result data is available.

knownBad.code: type ApiResult<T> = { data?: T; error?: string };
